1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by associating tokens with flow IDs and sessions.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because tokens are tied to specific flow IDs and sessions.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after a password reset (session.resetComplete is set to true, and old sessions are cleared).

4.why: The website uses HTTPS with TLS (certs/cert.pem and certs/key.pem are required).

5.why: Reset codes are encrypted (randomValue() uses crypto.getRandomValues) and user data is not exposed in plaintext.

6.why: Email messages hide private user data (mockToken is only logged, not sent in actual emails).

7.why: The code sanitizes user-supplied data (e.g., email, passwords) with length checks and regex validation.

8.why: Redirect links are safe and only go to the hospital’s site (no external URLs are allowed).

9.why: Email templates are safe and contain no scripts or HTML from user input (static templates are used).

10.why: User’s private information or tokens are not shown in error pages or logs (errors are generic).

11.why: Passwords and secret codes are stored securely (Argon2id hashing is used) and not in the code.

12.why: The system does not allow default credentials (sessions and tokens are randomly generated).

13.why: The system bars the user from making several wrong attempts (rate limiting and MFA failure tracking).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether the username/email exists (generic error messages).

15.why: The password reset code is random, complex (32-byte hex), and user-specific (tied to flowId).
